q: Why did our Google cost per click go up so much last week?
answer:
CPC on Google jumped from about ₹3 (previous week) to about ₹11 in 2026-10-19..2026-10-25 — roughly a +197% increase — and that came from two arithmetic effects, not a single proven cause.

- What changed (biggest movers): clicks fell 18,438 → 9,030 (−51.0%) while ad spend rose ₹62,933 → ₹92,699 (+47.3%). Those two together explain the CPC rise (clicks explain ~62% of the move; higher spend ~38%).
- Funnel and rate shifts: impressions dropped 5,26,717 → 4,03,859 (−23.3%) and CTR fell 3.5% → 2.2% (−36.1%). The exact decomposition shows Ad spend per impression rose ~92% and impressions-per-click rose ~57%; combined they produce the ~+200% CPC change.
- Mix effect: SEARCH campaigns expanded spend sharply (SEARCH spend +377%) and raised its share of volume; SEARCH CPC moved from ~₹19 → ~₹50 inside the window, so mix shifted toward higher-CPC campaign types.
- Cause confidence: the analysis found no single supported causal driver in the data (the result lists likely contributors and correlations but no tested cause). The data shows where and how it moved; it does not prove why.

Worth checking: the large SEARCH spend increase and why CTR dropped (creative/targeting or landing-page experience). 

Period: 2026-10-19..2026-10-25 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
